correctness.summary: Affine normalization reduces every half-plane target to the right half-plane, where the Paatero-Pinchuk L1 criterion applies. The nonlinear correction becomes Q+(1/c)zQ'/(Q+a) with c>0 and Re a>=0. A Stokes boundary-winding argument proves that this transform cannot decrease the circle L1 norm of Re Q, giving the required implication.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The 2013 paper explicitly poses the nonlinear implication as Problem 1; the 2014 erratum does not modify it; the 2017 Dziok-Noor paper restates a broader version and still calls beta!=0 open. Searches of the exact transform, bounded-Mocanu/boundary-rotation terminology, half-plane variants, and later citing literature did not locate the L1 contraction or this half-plane resolution.

value.summary: The result gives a nontrivial affirmative branch of a published nonlinear open problem for every half-plane target and all mu>=1, and supplies a reusable geometric contraction lemma explaining why the half-plane case is tractable.

limitations: Arbitrary convex target domains are not covered.
The two-distinct-target K_mu(H) problem from 2017 is not settled.
Equality cases of the contraction lemma are not classified.
Equivalent prior coverage under substantially different terminology may have escaped the search.
Independent audit has not been performed.
